condition: The tyre shows moderate exterior wear with accumulated dirt and weeds growing through the center, but the structural rubber tread remains intact.

safety.handling_warning: Wash hands thoroughly after handling due to outdoor dirt and potential stagnant water inside.

concepts.title: Patch Tread Puncture
concepts.description: Seal any minor punctures in the rubber casing to restore the tyre for non-vehicular utility uses.
steps: Clean the interior and exterior of the tyre thoroughly with water and a wire brush to remove all dirt and debris.
Locate the puncture site on the inner liner of the tyre.
Buff the area around the puncture with a rasp tool from the patch kit to roughen the vulcanised rubber.
Apply a thin, even layer of rubber cement over the buffed area and allow it to dry until tacky.
Press the rubber patch firmly over the hole, rolling it outward to eliminate any air bubbles.
Let the adhesive cure completely for 24 hours before loading the tyre.
concepts.image_prompt: A repaired black rubber car tyre with a neat patch visible on the inner wall, set against a plain neutral background with soft natural light.

concepts.title: Garden Planter
concepts.description: Transform the tyre into an elevated garden bed for growing flowers or ornamental plants.
steps: Clear all weeds and loose debris from inside the tyre cavity.
Position the tyre flat on level ground in your garden or courtyard.
Fill the bottom layer with coarse gravel or broken terracotta pieces for proper drainage.
Mix garden soil and organic compost in equal proportions.
Fill the tyre interior with the soil mixture up to two inches below the top rim.
Plant seasonal flower seeds or decorative shrubs into the soil and water gently.
concepts.image_prompt: A black rubber car tyre repurposed as a garden planter filled with rich brown soil and small green sprouts, set against a plain neutral background with soft natural light.

concepts.title: Jute-Woven Footstool
concepts.description: Wrap the outer rubber surface with natural jute rope to create a stylish rustic ottoman or footstool.
steps: Wash the tyre thoroughly and let it dry completely in the sun.
Cut two circular pieces of plywood to fit snugly over the top and bottom openings of the tyre.
Secure the top plywood lid to the tyre rim using heavy-duty construction adhesive or screws.
Start gluing natural jute rope at the center of the top wooden lid, spiraling outward to the edge.
Continue wrapping the jute rope tightly around the outer rubber sidewall of the tyre, securing with hot glue every few rotations.
Trim the rope cleanly and glue the final end neatly underneath the bottom edge.
Apply a clear protective sealant over the jute exterior for durability.
concepts.image_prompt: A rustic footstool made from a black rubber car tyre completely wrapped in tightly coiled natural brown jute rope, set against a plain neutral background with soft natural light.

recovery_plan.destination: local kabadiwala or authorised rubber recycler
